details:
Q1: Where should a demonstrated fix land? The pipeline can't push onto PR #6611's head branch directly.
Choices:
A. Open the fix PR against PR #6611's head branch, declared on a `Target branch: <PR #6611 head ref>` line in the issue body (`scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` routes to it). Fall back to the default branch if PR #6611 is already merged or closed. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Open the fix PR against the default branch, regardless of PR #6611's state.
C. Don't open a separate PR. Push straight onto PR #6611's head branch. This is outside the implement pipeline and needs an interactive session.
Q2: The implementer can't fetch job 113792812346's log or rerun CI. How should it get shard 1's failure?
Choices:
A. Rebuild shard 1 locally in the sandbox: run the same CI job slice at PR #6611's head with the same sharding variables (for `orchestrate-poll`: `CI_POLL_TEST_GROUP_INDEX` / `CI_POLL_TEST_GROUP_COUNT` / `CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS`). The fix PR's own CI run then serves as the "rerun CI" step. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Have a host-side step, or a person, paste shard 1's failing output into this issue first. Implementation waits until it's there.
C. Add a workflow step that fetches the job log with `GH_PAT` before the editor runs. This changes workflows beyond this triage.
Q3: If shard 1's failure doesn't reproduce, what should the run leave behind so it doesn't end as another no-op or BLOCKED?
Choices:
A. Commit only a short findings note, for example `docs/triage/pr-6611-ci-shard-1.md`, giving the PR head SHA, the exact commands run and the result. No code or workflow changes. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Make no commit. Close this issue as `ai:closed` with a findings comment and accept the no-op handling.
C. Emit `BLOCKED:` and hand the issue to a person.
